title: FlashAttention v3 autotuner + graded fallback strategy
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement an automatic kernel selection and tuning layer for FlashAttention v3 with a graded fallback strategy to v2 and generic kernels. Purpose: recover worst-case regressions observed when switching kernels, and extract consistent 10-30% token/sec improvements across shapes and GPU generations. The feature consists of: (1) an offline autotuner that generates a small lookup table of best kernel variants/tiling params per model shape and GPU; (2) an in-runtime selector that uses fast heuristics + telemetry to pick a kernel variant at prefill time and re-evaluate at decode boundaries; (3) a graded fallback policy with canary, degraded-mode thresholds, and an automatic rollback flow if QoS degrades.
acceptance_criteria: Autotuner populates lookup table for tested models (GPT-like: 1.3B, 7B, 33B) and GPUs (A100 40GB, H100 80GB)
Runtime selector chooses kernel variant on prefill with <2ms overhead per request for common batch sizes
Measured throughput improvement >=10% median and no >5% regression in P95 latency across test matrix compared to current baseline on our CI cluster
Canary rollout shows stable perf for 24h and automatic rollback triggers on sustained 7%+ unit-cost increase or 10%+ drop in token/sec over 10-minute window
Documentation and config UI entries in Console for enabling/disabling autotuner and tuning aggressiveness

test_matrix: Batch sizes: [1,2,4,8,16] for prefill; decode step steady-state batching up to 64 concurrent streams
GPU types: A100 40GB (Ampere), H100 80GB (Hopper), RTX 6000 Ada (Ampere/ADA) if available
Dtypes: fp16, bf16, int8-quantized kernel variants
Metrics: token/sec (throughput), p50/p95 latency per-token, memory consumption, unit-cost estimate, SLO violation counts
perf_findings: Preliminary autotuner runs (A100) show FlashAttention v3 tuned tiling gives +18% median token/sec for seq<=512 on 7B model vs baseline v2 kernels
On H100 for long sequences (seq 2048) some v3 tilings regress by ~6% token/sec due to L2 spilling; these shapes require conservative tiling or fallback to v2
Quantized int8 v3 path is promising for small models (1.3B) with 25-40% improvements but needs fast casting path to avoid decode overheads

Worst-case P95 latency regressions were observed when tiled kernels interact poorly with dynamic KV cache eviction; these were reproducible in CI and are addressed by inserting a lightweight cache-coherency check in selector logic
mitigation_plan: Introduce a graded fallback policy: try v3-fast -> v3-safe -> v2 -> generic. Each step increments conservatism and reduces tiling aggressiveness
Autotuner to emit a ‘safety_score’ per entry; runtime favors entries with higher safety when in high-SLO routes
Canary rollout on 5% of traffic with active telemetry tagging for kernel_variant. If 10-minute rolling averages cross thresholds, auto-disable autotuner and notify on-call
Add offline nightly regression job that compares token/sec delta per model/shape to detect silent degradations post-driver or dependency upgrades
Create a dev-runbook documenting how to reproduce regressions locally (CI job names, commands, PR templates)
